seoDescription: Learn how to create a stunning custom LED edge-lit sign using mirror acrylic. This detailed tutorial walks you through every step, from preparing materials to engraving an X-Men logo design. Discover the tools you'll need, including a Dremel engraver and a 12V LED strip light, and follow along to build a custom wooden base. This guide covers essential techniques like stenciling, engraving on the back of the mirror, assembling the base, and safely wiring the electronics for a professional finish.

summary:
## Project Overview
This guide details how to create a custom, edge-lit LED sign with an engraved X-Men logo on a mirror acrylic sheet, all housed in a handmade wooden base.

## Materials & Tools
- **Mirror Acrylic Sheet:** 3mm (1/8 inch) thick.
- **LEDs:** A 12V self-adhesive LED strip light tape.
- **Base:** Three lengths of square planed wood.
- **Engraver:** A Dremel engraver tool (reciprocating) is recommended for better control, but a Dremel drill with an engraving bit also works.
- **Stencil:** A design printed on thin cardboard and cut out with a sharp knife.
- **Router:** Used with roundover and 45-degree chamfer bits to shape the base.

## Engraving Process
1.  **Prepare the Stencil:** Carefully cut out the printed design to create a stencil.
2.  **Prepare the Acrylic:** Leave the protective film on the front (mirrored) side. The engraving is done on the back.
3.  **Position the Stencil:** Tape the stencil to the back of the acrylic sheet. The stencil image must be inverted (mirrored) so it appears correctly from the front.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Always engrave on the **back** of the mirror sheet and use a **reversed** stencil. Failure to do so will result in a backward image.

4.  **Engrave:** Wear a dust mask for safety. Practice on scrap acrylic to get a feel for the tool. Engraving along the tops of letters first helps maintain alignment.

## Building the Wooden Base
- **Construction:** The base consists of three wooden pieces that form a slot to hold the acrylic and house the LED strip.
- **Wood Shaping:**
    - Use a **router** with a **roundover bit** to soften the top edges of all three pieces.
    - Use a **45-degree chamfer bit** on one bottom edge of each of the two side pieces. When placed together, these create the V-groove for the LED strip.
- **Assembly Steps:**
    1.  Adhere the **LED strip** to the centerline of the main base piece.
    2.  Apply wood glue, position one side piece using the acrylic for spacing, and clamp it down.
    3.  For extra strength, drill pilot holes and secure the side piece with **screws** from the bottom.
    4.  Repeat the process for the second side piece.
    5.  Once the glue is dry, apply **varnish** to the finished base.

## Wiring & Power
- **Power Requirements:** The LED strip requires a specific voltage (e.g., 12V). The power supply must match this voltage and provide at least the required amperage (e.g., a 1A supply is sufficient for a 0.15A strip).
- **Connection:** A **DC barrel jack adapter** with screw terminals offers a simple, solder-free way to connect the power supply to the LED strip's wires.

> [!NOTE]
> The LED strip is polarity-sensitive. If it doesn't turn on, simply reverse the positive and negative wires in the screw terminal. This will not damage the LEDs.

## Final Assembly
1.  Leave a small amount of protective film on the bottom of the acrylic sheet to prevent scratches while inserting it into the base.
2.  Slide the engraved acrylic into the slot in the base.
3.  Remove the remaining film.
4.  Plug in the power supply to light up your new sign.
transcription:
## Introduction & Materials

Hello and welcome back to TechyDIY. In today's video, I'm going to show you how to make an X-Men LED mirror sign.

The materials that I've used are an acrylic mirror sheet. This is 3 millimeters thick, which is about one-eighth of an inch. A 12-volt strip light tape. You can buy these in various lengths, and they consist of a flexible PCB with self-adhesive backing. The tape has multiple sections, each containing three LEDs and a resistor. You can cut the tape to length at the marked positions and solder on some connecting wires or buy them already cut to length with the wires attached.

I've also used three lengths of square planed wood. To engrave the design, I've used a Dremel engraver tool, but you can also use a Dremel drill with an engraving bit. The difference between the two is that the Dremel engraver has a reciprocating action while the drill rotates. This means that the engraver is a little bit easier to control.

The X-Men design is printed onto thin cardboard, and this is cut out to make a stencil. The stencil image is available to download from my website, and the link for this is listed in the video description along with all the parts and tools used in this project.

## Creating the Stencil

To cut out the stencil, we need a sharp knife and a surface to work on. I'm using a self-healing cutting mat, which is a great way of protecting the work surface. To ensure the cuts are straight, I'm also using a ruler.

## Engraving the Acrylic Mirror

The mirror is engraved on the back, so leave the protective film on the mirrored side and turn the sheet upside down. The stencil also needs to be inverted, otherwise the letters will be reversed when viewed from the front. Use tape to firmly attach the stencil on all four sides.

The engraving process creates a fine dust, so as a precaution, I'm wearing a dust mask. Before starting to engrave, it's a good idea to practice on some scrap material just to get a feel for the engraver. A good place to start engraving is along the top of the letters. If you engrave them in one go, then it helps to keep the letters level with each other.

## Shaping the Wooden Base

The next task is to make the base. This is quite simple and consists of three pieces of wood glued together to form a slot with the LED strip in the center. Cut the wood for the base to the correct length, and then with a roundover bit in the router, round over the top edges. Take the uncut length of wood allocated for the sides and round over the top two edges.

Change the router bit to a 45-degree chamfer bit and then chamfer one of the bottom edges. Cut the wood to form two side pieces. To improve the finish, sand the wood with 240 grit sandpaper. The final profile of the wood pieces look like this. You can see the V-groove at the bottom ready to accommodate the LED strip.

## Assembling the Base

Next, mark the center line on the base. Remove the backing from the LED strip and apply it using a ruler to achieve a straight line.

Place the acrylic mirror sheet onto the line of LEDs. Hold the side against the acrylic sheet and mark its position. Apply wood glue to the base and side. Place the side in position, and using the second side for support, apply clamps. Adjust the position and then wipe away any excess glue with a damp cloth.

For additional strength, drill three pilot holes through the base and into the side. Countersink the holes and then attach with three screws. Place the acrylic mirror sheet back onto the LEDs. Place the second side against the acrylic sheet and then clamp it into position. Drill pilot holes through the base and into the second side. Countersink the holes and attach the second side with three screws.

## Finishing and Final Assembly

Remove the clamp and the acrylic mirror sheet. Apply varnish and leave the completed base to dry.

Using gloves, remove the protective film from the mirror sheet. Leave about an inch of film so that the mirrored surface is protected when it's placed into the base. And finally, place the mirror sheet into the base.

## Wiring the LED Power

The final task is to connect the LED strip to a power supply. The LED strip specification should list the supply voltage and either the current or power in watts. The LED strip that I've used requires 12 volts at 0.15 amps. The power supply comes from some disused equipment, and it can supply 12 volts at 1 amp.

To connect the power supply to the LED strip, we could cut off the connector and join the wires together using a chock block or by soldering, but what I'm going to do is use one of these adapters which has a screw connection on one side and a DC socket on the other. The LED strip will only work if the positive and negative from the supply are correctly connected. However, it won't do any damage if you do get it the wrong way around. That's the LED mirror completed, and now we just need to plug it in.

## Final Reveal and Conclusion

I hope you enjoyed this video. I'm really pleased with how the project turned out. The mirrored acrylic works really well. If you liked this project, then you might like some of my others, so please subscribe and check out my other videos. Thanks for watching, and I'll see you again next time.
